name: Pitch Shifter
description: Two pitch-shifted voices in three characters, clean, grainy or fluttering, with a delay and feedback that make the repeats climb or fall.

params.name: Pitch A
params.description: The interval of the first voice above or below what is played. It glides when moved, so it can be played like a pitch pedal.

params.name: Pitch B
params.description: The interval of the second voice. It is silent until Voice B is raised.

params.name: Voice B
params.description: How loud the second voice is beside the first. Zero leaves a single shifted voice.

params.name: Detune
params.description: Pushes voice A a little sharp and voice B a little flat. With both pitches at zero it is a doubler that thickens the sound.

params.name: Mode
params.description: The character of the shift. Smooth lines its splices up with the sound and stays clean, Grain rebuilds it from overlapping grains, Vintage splices blindly and flutters like an early digital pitch changer.

params.name: Size
params.description: The length of the pieces the sound is cut into. Short is tight in time and rough, down to a metallic buzz in Grain; long is smoother and trails further behind the playing.

params.name: Jitter
params.description: Scatters each piece in time and pitch. A little loosens the shift like a chorus; a lot turns it into a noisy cloud, widest in Grain, where the grains are also thrown left and right.

params.name: Delay
params.description: How late the shifted voices arrive. With Feedback it is the gap between repeats.

params.name: Feedback
params.description: Sends the shifted voices back in through the delay, so each repeat is shifted again and climbs or falls. With no delay it thickens into a shimmer.

params.name: Tone
params.description: Darkens the shifted voices. It sits in the feedback path too, so each repeat is duller than the last.

params.name: Spread
params.description: Moves voice A to the left and voice B to the right. A voice on its own stays in the middle.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Balance between the dry signal and the shifted voices.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. Models the delay-line pitch changers and harmonizers of the late 1970s and the grain shifters that followed, in outline, not any one unit: two voices of read heads on a shared ring of recent input, with a delay and feedback so that repeats are shifted again. Smooth places each new head by normalised cross-correlation with the one it takes over from, the autocorrelation de-glitch splice of US patent 4,464,784 (expired) and the alignment step of WSOLA (W. Verhelst and M. Roelands, 'An overlap-add technique based on waveform similarity (WSOLA) for high quality time-scale modification of speech', ICASSP 1993). Vintage is pitch shifting by delay-line modulation with two crossfaded taps (P. Dutilleux, G. De Poli and U. Zölzer, 'Time-segment processing', in DAFX: Digital Audio Effects, 2002). Grain is overlap-add of Hann grains read at the shifted rate with randomised onsets (R. Bencina, 'Implementing real-time granular synthesis', 2001).
